R6K-bear-walk-0002.name: 130 m NE of Sphaler Creek
R6K-bear-walk-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R6K-bear-walk-0002.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burn from 2019 (fire R90918), 440 m E: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 36 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Sphaler Creek 130 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Stewart, about 172 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 57.04262, -131.26352, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 390 m NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 61 m, about 14 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-21, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2018-12-18, closures 2026-10-16.
R6K-bear-walk-0002.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-21: about 6 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.00 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.4 km and about 61 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
